title: Wedding guest (Western)
text: Follow the invitation dress code. Cocktail attire: tailored suit in navy, charcoal or mid-grey with a light shirt and tie, or a knee-to-midi dress. Avoid white, ivory or anything that could upstage the couple. Evening weddings allow darker colours and richer fabrics like velvet; daytime and outdoor weddings suit linen, pastels and lighter suiting.

title: Pakistani / South Asian wedding events
text: Mehndi: bright yellows, greens and oranges; embroidered kurta with shalwar or churidar, or a colourful lehenga. Barat: the most formal event; sherwani or prince coat for men, heavily embellished outfits in deep reds, maroons and golds for women. Walima: softer and more elegant; pastels, silver and champagne tones, waistcoat over kurta, or a lighter formal. Khussa or peshawari chappal complete the look.

title: Job interview
text: Dress one step above the company's daily dress code. Corporate: a well-fitted navy or charcoal suit, white or light-blue shirt, minimal accessories. Tech and start-ups: smart casual, such as a blazer over a plain knit or crisp shirt with dark chinos or tailored trousers and clean leather shoes. Fit matters more than price.

title: Smart casual
text: Mix one tailored piece with relaxed ones: an unstructured blazer with a T-shirt or fine-knit turtleneck, dark jeans or chinos, loafers or minimal leather sneakers. Keep the palette to 2-3 colours. A black turtleneck with a navy or camel blazer is a timeless combination.

title: Streetwear
text: Built on proportion: oversized hoodies or boxy tees over wide or cargo pants, balanced by chunky sneakers such as Jordan 4s, New Balance or Salomons. Layer with a coach jacket, puffer or overshirt. Earth tones, washed black and a single accent colour keep it cohesive. A cap, crossbody bag or chain adds finish.

title: University / everyday casual
text: Comfort first but intentional: a clean hoodie or crewneck sweater, straight-leg jeans, and white sneakers. For presentations, swap the hoodie for an overshirt or knit polo. In warm weather, a linen shirt or cotton kurta with chinos works well.

title: Dressing for hot weather
text: Breathable natural fabrics: linen, cotton lawn, seersucker. Lighter colours reflect heat. Loose silhouettes such as camp-collar shirts, wide trousers and lawn suits keep air moving. Sunglasses and a hat double as protection. Avoid polyester and heavy denim.

title: Winter layering
text: Three layers: a base (tee or thermal), an insulating mid layer (merino sweater, cardigan or fleece) and an outer shell (overcoat, puffer or parka). A long camel or charcoal overcoat instantly smartens any outfit. Add a scarf in a contrasting texture and leather boots.

title: Colour matching basics
text: Navy, grey, white, black, olive and camel are neutrals that pair with almost anything. Use the 60-30-10 rule: a dominant colour, a secondary and a small accent. Warm undertones suit earthy tones, gold and cream; cool undertones suit jewel tones, silver and pure white. Monochrome outfits in one colour family look elongating and polished.

title: Trends: Autumn/Winter 2026
text: Key directions this season: relaxed tailoring with wider trousers and softer shoulders; chocolate brown and burgundy as the new neutrals; suede and brushed textures; oversized leather and bomber jackets; quiet-luxury knitwear; loafers with chunky soles; and utility details such as pockets and belts on outerwear.

title: Trends: Spring/Summer 2026
text: Seasonal highlights: butter yellow and powder blue pastels, sheer layering, relaxed linen suiting, boxy short-sleeve shirts, fisherman sandals and retro running sneakers, plus crochet and open-weave knits for resortwear.

title: Party / night out
text: Lean into texture and a bit of shine: satin or silk shirts, leather jackets, sequins or velvet. A dark base (black trousers or jeans) lets one statement piece stand out. Chelsea boots or clean sneakers depending on the venue.

title: Eid and festive occasions
text: Crisp shalwar kameez or kurta pajama in white, pastel or jewel tones, often with a contrasting waistcoat. Chikankari and subtle thread embroidery are timeless. Women's festive wear ranges from embroidered lawn and chiffon suits to anarkalis. Finish with khussa, a watch or light jewellery.

title: Fit fundamentals
text: Shoulder seams should sit at the shoulder bone; sleeves should show a little shirt cuff; trousers should have minimal break. Balance proportions: pair a loose top with a slimmer bottom or vice versa. A defined waist such as a tucked shirt or a belt adds structure to any outfit.
